prompt: A single tower arcology, every floor a different district.

lots.label: arcology tower
lots.brief: One huge tower holding the whole city as stacked floors, each its own district with its own palette and lighting, linked by a central stairwell and shafts. Shell of stone, glass and iron, glass-crowned top. Floors from the bottom: market (stalls, shops, tavern under lanterns), residential (small apartments along corridors), hydroponic farm (crop beds, water channels, glowstone), forge and workshop (smithies, smelters), temple and garden (open-air garden, chapel), observatory (glass dome).

lots.label: ground-level gatehouse and lobby
lots.brief: Entrance plaza at the tower base, leading to the central stairwell.

rules.label: Districts stacked as floors of one tower
rules.notes: Six district floors (market, residential, farm, workshop, garden/temple, observatory) stacked in one volume.

plan.notes: The tower is a single lot; its stacked district floors are a reserved rule and wait.

waits.words: The stacked district floors inside the tower wait for a later Architect release; the tower shell and gatehouse are built first.

answer.summary: The Stacked City is one huge central tower on level ground, with a gatehouse and lobby plaza at its base. I wrote the tower as a single landmark building, and its six district floors (market, residential, farm, workshop, garden and temple, observatory) as a stacked-floors rule. Architect can't build that rule yet, so the floors wait while the tower and gatehouse go first.
